hints: Look closely at the units in each option, three are in nm and only one is in µm. Remember that 1 µm is 1000 times bigger than 1 nm, so which one is truly huge?
A light microscope using visible light cannot separate objects closer than about 200 nm. Which of the four sizes is comfortably larger than this resolution limit?
walkthrough:
**Remember what limits a light microscope**

Think of resolution as the smallest gap your microscope can still see as separate. For visible light, that limit is set by the wavelength of light.

Key rule to remember:
$$\text{light microscope resolution} \approx 200 \, nm$$

**Compare each size to that limit**

Let's put everything in the same units. The Paramecium is very large:
$$200 \, \mu m = 200 \times 1000 \, nm = 200,000 \, nm$$
That is 1000 times bigger than the 200 nm limit, so it will be easily seen. The other three are 2 nm, 8 nm and 20 nm, all smaller than 200 nm.

**Choose the visible structure**

Anything smaller than about 200 nm is blurred out with light and needs an electron microscope. Only the Paramecium cell is big enough for a school light microscope with natural light, so B is the answer.

options.A: A 2 nm DNA molecule is 100 times smaller than the 200 nm resolution limit, so it cannot be resolved with light and needs an electron microscope.
options.B: A 200 µm Paramecium is about 200,000 nm, far larger than the 200 nm limit, so its whole cell and cilia are easily visible with a light microscope.
options.C: An 8 nm phospholipid bilayer is far below the 200 nm limit, so it is invisible with light and only seen with an electron microscope.
options.D: A 20 nm ribosome is still 10 times smaller than the 200 nm limit, so it cannot be resolved with a light microscope.
